```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(osmactive)
library(tidyr)
library(gganimate)
library(gifski)
library(knitr)

years = 2019:2025
data_dir = "data-raw"
dir.create(data_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Ensure per-year classified GeoPackage snapshots (2019-2025) and England baseline are present
release_base = "https://github.com/nptscot/osmactive/releases/download/coventry-viz"

for (yr in years) {
  gpkg_file = file.path(data_dir, sprintf("coventry-cycleways-%d.gpkg", yr))
  if (!file.exists(gpkg_file)) {
    download.file(
      sprintf("%s/coventry-cycleways-%d.gpkg", release_base, yr),
      gpkg_file,
      mode = "wb",
      quiet = TRUE
    )
  }
}

england_rds = file.path(data_dir, "england_cycleway_growth.rds")
if (!file.exists(england_rds)) {
  download.file(
    sprintf("%s/england_cycleway_growth.rds", release_base),
    england_rds,
    mode = "wb",
    quiet = TRUE
  )
}

infra_levels = c(
  "Segregated Track (wide)",
  "Off Road Path",
  "Segregated Track (narrow)",
  "Shared Footway",
  "Painted Cycle Lane"
)

# Read and combine per-year snapshots (2019-2025), keeping core attributes + geometry
cycle_list = lapply(years, function(yr) {
  gpkg_file = file.path(data_dir, sprintf("coventry-cycleways-%d.gpkg", yr))
  d = st_read(gpkg_file, quiet = TRUE)
  d$seg_length_m = as.numeric(st_length(d))
  d |>
    select(
      osm_id,
      name,
      highway,
      cycle_segregation,
      detailed_segregation,
      width_clean,
      distance_to_road,
      seg_length_m
    ) |>
    mutate(
      year = as.integer(yr),
      cycle_segregation = factor(cycle_segregation, levels = infra_levels)
    )
})

cycle_data = bind_rows(cycle_list)
```

# Introduction

This repository provides a reproducible analysis of the growth of cycling infrastructure in Coventry from 2019 to 2025.

We compare a simple metric based solely on the `highway=cycleway` OpenStreetMap (OSM) tag with the multi-layered classification system implemented in the [`osmactive`](https://github.com/nptscot/osmactive) R package.

# Detailed Infrastructure Growth (2019–2025)

The following code chunk and plot show the annual growth of the Coventry cycle network across the specified years (`2019:2025`), broken down by `osmactive` infrastructure categories.

```{r stacked-bar}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

stacked_data = cycle_data |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(year, cycle_segregation) |>
  summarise(
    length_km = sum(seg_length_m, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  complete(year = years, cycle_segregation = factor(infra_levels, levels = infra_levels), fill = list(length_km = 0)) |>
  mutate(cycle_segregation = factor(cycle_segregation, levels = rev(infra_levels)))

p_stacked = ggplot(stacked_data, aes(x = factor(year), y = length_km, fill = cycle_segregation)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = rev(get_palette_npt()), name = "Infrastructure Type") +
  labs(
    title = "Coventry Cycle Network Growth by Type (2019-2025)",
    subtitle = "Annual historical snapshots classified using osmactive",
    y = "Total Length (km)",
    x = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1)
  )

ggsave("coventry_growth_chart.png", p_stacked, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

![Coventry Cycle Network Growth by Type (2019-2025).](https://github.com/itsleeds/infra_aq/releases/download/v0.1.0/coventry_growth_chart.png)

```{r summary-table}
summary_table = stacked_data |>
  mutate(cycle_segregation = factor(cycle_segregation, levels = infra_levels)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = cycle_segregation, values_from = length_km) |>
  mutate(
    Total = rowSums(across(all_of(infra_levels))),
    across(where(is.numeric) & !c(year), \(x) round(x, 2))
  ) |>
  rename(Year = year)

kable(summary_table, caption = "Classified cycling infrastructure length (km) in Coventry by year and type (2019-2025).")
```

## Animated Growth Map

The spatial expansion of Coventry's cycling network across `2019:2025` is generated reproducibly below using `gganimate` and `gifski`:

```{r animate-map}
anim_data = cycle_data |>
  mutate(
    display_year = as.integer(year),
    cycle_segregation = factor(cycle_segregation, levels = infra_levels)
  )

infra_colors = get_palette_npt()

p_anim = ggplot(anim_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(color = cycle_segregation), linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = infra_colors, drop = FALSE) +
  transition_manual(display_year) +
  labs(
    title = "Coventry Cycle Network Growth: {current_frame}",
    subtitle = "Year-by-year classified infrastructure (2019-2025)",
    color = "Infrastructure Type",
    caption = "Data: OpenStreetMap contributors (Geofabrik January snapshots)"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )

anim = animate(
  p_anim,
  nframes = length(years),
  fps = 1,
  renderer = gifski_renderer(),
  width = 800,
  height = 600,
  units = "px"
)
anim_save("coventry_historical_growth.gif", animation = anim)
```

![Animation showing Coventry Cycle Network Growth from 2019 to 2025.](https://github.com/itsleeds/infra_aq/releases/download/v0.1.0/coventry_historical_growth.gif)

# Simple Metric (`highway=cycleway`) and National Comparison

A common approach to quantifying cycling infrastructure is to filter for segments where the `highway` tag is explicitly set to `cycleway`. Below we compare Coventry's `highway=cycleway` growth from 2019 to 2025 against the national trend for England (indexed to 2019 = 100).

```{r national-comparison}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

england_growth = readRDS(england_rds) |>
  filter(year %in% years) |>
  arrange(year) |>
  mutate(index = length_km / first(length_km) * 100, region = "England")

cov_simple = cycle_data |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(highway == "cycleway") |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(length_km = sum(seg_length_m, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000, .groups = "drop") |>
  complete(year = years, fill = list(length_km = 0)) |>
  arrange(year) |>
  mutate(index = length_km / first(length_km) * 100, region = "Coventry")

comparison = bind_rows(
  england_growth |> select(year, length_km, index, region),
  cov_simple |> select(year, length_km, index, region)
)

p_comp = ggplot(comparison, aes(x = year, y = index, color = region)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = years) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(95, NA)) +
  labs(
    title = "Relative Growth of Cycling Infrastructure: Coventry vs. England (2019-2025)",
    subtitle = "Index (2019 = 100) based on highway=cycleway length",
    y = "Growth Index (2019 = 100)",
    x = "Year",
    color = "Region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("coventry_vs_england.png", p_comp, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

![Relative Growth of Cycling Infrastructure: Coventry vs. England (2019-2025).](https://github.com/itsleeds/infra_aq/releases/download/v0.1.0/coventry_vs_england.png)

Between 2019 and 2025, England's `highway=cycleway` network grew by approximately `r round(last(england_growth$index) - 100)`%, whereas Coventry's dedicated `highway=cycleway` network grew by `r round(last(cov_simple$index) - 100)`% (from `r round(first(cov_simple$length_km), 1)` km in 2019 to `r round(last(cov_simple$length_km), 1)` km in 2025). Across all `osmactive` cycle infrastructure categories, Coventry's network expanded by `r round((last(summary_table$Total) / first(summary_table$Total) - 1) * 100)`% (from `r round(first(summary_table$Total), 1)` km in 2019 to `r round(last(summary_table$Total), 1)` km in 2025).
